title: White Chicken Chili Crock
seoTitle: White Chicken Chili Crock | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Creamy bean-and-chicken chili for ten
description: Chicken, white beans, green chiles, corn, and a creamy broth cook into a filling chili.

steps.title: Morning start
steps.instruction: Place chicken in the slow cooker with beans, green chiles, broth, cumin, and onion.

steps.title: Set heat
steps.instruction: Cover and cook on low for 7 hours; keep the cooker plugged into a stable outlet.

steps.title: Check chicken
steps.instruction: At dinner time, check the thickest breast has reached at least 165°F before shredding.

steps.title: Shred chicken
steps.instruction: Lift chicken to a clean tray, shred it with forks, and return it to the hot chili.

steps.title: Add corn
steps.instruction: Stir in frozen corn so it heats through without becoming dull and soft.

steps.title: Melt cream cheese
steps.instruction: Add cubed cream cheese and stir every few minutes until no white lumps remain.

steps.title: Adjust thickness
steps.instruction: Mash one cup of beans against the pot wall if the chili needs more body.

steps.title: Taste carefully
steps.instruction: Taste only with a clean spoon, then add salt or lime without over-salting canned beans.

steps.title: Hold chili
steps.instruction: Switch to warm after it is steaming hot; verify it stays above 140°F.

steps.title: Serve bowls
steps.instruction: Ladle chili into bowls and let crew add cheese, cilantro, chips, and lime.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Chicken breasts — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Chicken breasts and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Keep dairy out until the final hour.
Use two ladles so toppings stay separate.
Thin with hot broth, not cold water.
tonightSpread: Condiments: shredded cheese, cilantro, lime wedges
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Chicken breasts in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is economical, holds well, and toppings make it work for different appetites.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: measure spices and drain beans the night before. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: bring chili and chicken to 165°F.
substitutions: Use coconut milk for cream cheese.
